title: Armavia 967

agencies.name: Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety

summary: Armavia Flight 967 was attempting a go-around following its first approach to Sochi airport at night with weather below landing minimums. While performing the climb with the autopilot disengaged, the captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness. The insufficient pitch-control inputs led to failure to recover the aircraft and it crashed into the sea. All 113 aboard were killed.
probable_cause: The captain, being in a psychoemotional stress condition, made nose-down control inputs due to the loss of pitch and roll awareness while performing the climb after an aborted approach. The first officer's lack of monitoring the aircraft's pitch attitude and altitude, and no proper reaction to GPWS warnings, contributed to the crash.

factors.evidence: The captain lost pitch and roll awareness while performing the climb with autopilot disengaged.
The captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness.
The first officer failed to monitor the aircraft's pitch attitude, altitude, and vertical speed.
There was no proper reaction by the crew to GPWS warnings.
The aircraft crashed into the sea while conducting a climbing maneuver after an aborted approach.

events.text: The airplane took off from Zvartnots airport at 20:47 with 113 occupants on board
Crew decided to continue the flight to Sochi airport at 21:31
Crew reported gear down and ready for landing, then performed go-around after overshooting the runway extended centreline
During climb with autopilot disengaged, captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness
GPWS warnings sounded during the climb
The aircraft crashed into the sea after the crew's insufficient pitch-control inputs led to failure to recover

title: S7 Airlines 778
summary: Airbus A310 overran the runway during landing at Irkutsk after the captain unintentionally moved the left engine throttle lever forward while attempting to reduce reverse thrust on the right engine. The first officer, distracted by a spurious takeoff warning, failed to monitor engine parameters and did not detect the error until insufficient runway remained to stop. The aircraft crashed through the airport's concrete perimeter fence, struck rows of private garages, and burst into flames. The investigation concluded pilot error was the cause, with inadequate crew coordination enabling the control error to progress to runway overrun.
probable_cause: The captain inadvertently moved the left engine throttle forward while reducing the right engine's reverse thrust, causing the left engine to produce significant forward thrust instead of reverse thrust. The first officer failed to monitor engine parameters and did not detect the error. The crew's poor coordination resulted in inability to resolve the issue before overrunning the runway.

factors.evidence: Captain unintentionally moved the left engine throttle lever forward while attempting to reduce the right engine's reverse thrust.
Co-pilot failed to monitor engine parameters and was distracted by spurious takeoff warning on ECAM display.
Crew failed to realize the source of the problem and were unable to resolve the issue once the engine thrust configuration error occurred.
Aircraft overran the runway with only 800 meters remaining of runway asphalt remaining.
Aircraft burst into flames after crashing through perimeter fence and striking garages.

events.text: Aircraft touches down on runway, captain arms spoilers and engages autobrake to low mode, right engine reverser deployed to maximum.
Spurious takeoff warning alert appears on ECAM cockpit display during landing roll.
First officer attempts multiple times to erase spurious warning from ECAM cockpit monitor, becoming distracted from monitoring engine parameters.
While reducing right engine reverse thrust, captain unintentionally moves left engine throttle lever forward.
Left engine produces significant forward thrust instead of reverse thrust, aircraft begins accelerating instead of decelerating.
Captain notices aircraft did not slow down and asks first officer about RPM increasing and what is happening.
Captain orders right engine thrust reverser deployed again to maximum, but only 800 meters of runway remaining.
Aircraft overruns runway end, crashes through concrete perimeter fence, strikes rows of garages, and bursts into flames.

title: Pulkovo Aviation Enterprise 612
summary: Tu-154M departed Anapa and half an hour later encountered severe thunderstorms and turbulence in the vicinity while en route to Saint Petersburg. At 15:33, the crew requested and received permission to climb to 39,000 feet. At 15:35:02, the crew disengaged the autopilot during high-altitude flight. Almost immediately, the stall warning sounded with the angle of attack increasing to 46 degrees while forward airspeed dropped to zero. The aircraft entered a deep stall with pitch oscillations exceeding operational range limits from which the crew could not recover. The flight crashed 45 km northwest of Donetsk near the village of Sukha Balka killing all 170 people on board.
probable_cause: Aircraft flown in manual flight mode at high altitude with excessive angles of attack causing a stall with transition to flat spin. Flight manual and crew training programs did not provide instruction on manual pitch control and pitch trim during high-altitude flight. Lack of appropriate high-altitude stall recovery simulators contributed to crew's inability to recover from the stall.

factors.evidence: stall warning sounded and flight's angle of attack increased to 46 degrees while forward airspeed dropped to zero

Flight manual and crew training programs did not provide instruction on manual pitch control and pitch trim during high-altitude flight and the lack of appropriate simulators contributed to crew inability
there were thunderstorms in the vicinity of the flight and the aircraft entered an area of severe turbulence
while avoiding areas of thunderstorms and turbulence the crew allowed the aircraft to enter pitch oscillations exceeding the angle of attack operational range
poor crew resource management allowed the situation to escalate into a catastrophic one
aircraft entered deep stall and transitioned to flat spin from which the crew could not recover and collided with ground at high vertical speed

At 15:33, the crew requested and received permission to climb to 39,000 feet to avoid thunderstorms
At 15:35:02, the crew disengaged the autopilot at high altitude during manual flight in turbulent conditions
